# Behavioral Specification: Entropy Source Core

## 1. Overview

The entropy source core is the main processing block of the entropy source IP. It receives raw entropy samples from an external physical random number generator, applies continuous health testing, optionally conditions the tested entropy using a cryptographic conditioner, and makes complete entropy seeds available to either a hardware consumer or firmware.

The module operates in several modes:

- Conditioned (FIPS) mode: raw entropy is health tested, accumulated, and cryptographically conditioned into full-entropy seeds.
- Bypass mode: health-tested raw entropy is packed into seeds without cryptographic conditioning.
- Firmware override mode: firmware can observe raw entropy, insert its own entropy, and optionally use the hardware conditioner.
- Software route mode: generated seeds are directed to a firmware-readable 32-bit interface instead of the hardware interface.

The module also provides recoverable and fatal alert outputs, four interrupt outputs, an external vendor health-test interface, and OTP-gated configuration controls.

## 2. Reset and Initialization

On reset:

- The module must be fully disabled.
- All internal storage must be empty.
- No entropy seeds shall be presented on any output interface.
- The RNG enable output must be deasserted.
- All interrupt outputs must be inactive.
- All alert outputs must be inactive.

After reset, the module shall remain idle until firmware enables it through the register interface. Configuration writes shall have no effect unless the software update lock is opened and the module is not running.

## 3. Configuration and Register Locking

The module must enforce the following configuration rules:

- Configuration and control registers shall only be writable when a software update enable field is set.
- Configuration writes shall only be accepted while the module is disabled and no internal processing from a previous enabled period is still draining.
- Once the module is enabled, configuration registers shall be locked. They shall remain locked until the module is disabled and has completed all in-flight processing.
- The module-enable field and all security-sensitive control fields use multi-bit encoded values. If any such field contains an invalid encoding, the module shall treat the field as disabled or false and shall raise a recoverable alert with a corresponding status indication.

When the module-enable field is asserted:

- The module shall first generate an internal initialization event that clears health-test state and counters.
- After that initialization event, normal entropy collection and processing shall begin.

## 4. Operating Modes

### 4.1 Conditioned (FIPS) Mode

In conditioned mode:

- Raw entropy from the RNG interface is health tested.
- Health-tested entropy is accumulated until enough data is available for the cryptographic conditioner.
- The conditioner produces a complete 384-bit entropy seed.
- Each seed is tagged with a FIPS-compliance indication.
- The FIPS tag shall be asserted only when the seed was produced in conditioned mode, the module is fully enabled, and full-width RNG samples are used.
- If single-bit RNG sampling is enabled, seeds may still be conditioned but shall not be tagged as FIPS-compliant.

### 4.2 Bypass Mode

Bypass mode is used for boot-time entropy or when firmware performs its own conditioning.

The module shall operate in bypass mode when:

- FIPS compliance mode is disabled, or
- The software route is selected and the entropy type is configured to use the bypass path.

In bypass mode:

- Raw entropy is health tested in the same manner as in conditioned mode.
- Health-tested entropy is packed directly into 384-bit seeds without passing through the cryptographic conditioner.
- Bypass seeds shall not carry the FIPS-compliance tag.

### 4.3 Firmware Override Mode

Firmware override mode has two sub-functions:

1. **Entropy observation**: health-tested raw entropy is simultaneously written into an observation FIFO that firmware can read. This allows firmware to perform additional health checks. The module shall indicate when the observation FIFO has reached a programmed threshold. If the observation FIFO overflows, the module shall set an overflow status; after an overflow, no new data shall be written to the FIFO until it has been fully drained.

2. **Entropy insertion**: firmware can write 32-bit words back into the entropy pipeline. Inserted entropy shall be inserted after the hardware health-test stage, so it is not subject to the hardware health tests. The inserted words are sent either to the conditioning path or to the bypass seed-packing path, depending on the selected mode.

The module shall expose a full status for the firmware insertion path. A write attempted while the insertion path is full shall trigger a recoverable alert and the written data shall not be accepted.

When the firmware override insertion path is used with the hardware conditioner, the module shall support a start/stop control for the conditioner. If firmware disables the SHA3 insertion operation while data is still present in the pipeline, the module shall:

- Assert a recoverable alert.
- Mark any affected in-flight seeds as invalid.
- Prevent those invalid seeds from being delivered to any output interface.

Firmware override functions shall only be operational when the corresponding OTP enable input is asserted. If OTP disables firmware override, all firmware override controls shall have no effect.

### 4.4 Software Route Mode

When the software entropy route is selected:

- Generated seeds shall be moved from the final seed storage into a 32-bit unpacking path for firmware reads.
- The hardware entropy interface shall not be served while software routing is selected; hardware requests shall wait until software routing is disabled.
- An interrupt shall indicate when at least one 32-bit word of entropy is available for firmware.
- A complete 384-bit seed is consumed over twelve 32-bit reads.
- The firmware read path shall only operate when the corresponding OTP enable input and the entropy-data-register enable field are both asserted. If either is not asserted, reads of the entropy data register shall return zeros and shall not pop data from the FIFO.

## 5. RNG Input and Sampling

The RNG interface supplies raw entropy as 4-bit samples with a validity indication.

Behavior:

- When the module is enabled and its input storage is not full, the module shall assert the RNG enable output.
- The module shall accept a raw entropy sample only when both the RNG enable output is asserted and the RNG validity signal is asserted.
- If the input storage becomes full, the module shall deassert RNG enable to provide backpressure to the RNG source.
- When disabled, the module shall deassert RNG enable and shall ignore incoming RNG samples.

The module may be configured to use single-bit sampling. When single-bit sampling is enabled:

- The module shall select one of the four input lanes according to the configured bit selection.
- It shall pack four selected bits into one 4-bit symbol for health testing.
- The FIPS-compliance tag shall be suppressed for seeds generated while single-bit sampling is active.

## 6. Health Testing

All raw entropy received from the RNG interface shall be subjected to health testing before it is stored or forwarded. Firmware-inserted entropy is exempt because it enters downstream of the health-test stage.

The module shall continuously perform these health tests:

- **Repetition Count Test**: detects excessive consecutive equal values in each bit lane. This test is not window-based; it operates continuously across window boundaries.
- **Repetition Count Symbol Test**: detects excessive repetition of the same multi-bit symbol.
- **Adaptive Proportion Test**: counts the number of ones in a window of samples and checks whether the count is within configured high and low thresholds.
- **Bucket Test**: classifies each multi-bit symbol into a bucket and detects bias in the symbol distribution.
- **Markov Test**: detects unexpected first-order correlation between consecutive samples by comparing the number of transitions against configured high and low thresholds.
- **External Vendor Health Test**: the module provides the raw entropy sample stream and test-control information to an external health-test block through the vendor health-test interface, and receives test counts and failure indications back.

### 6.1 Health-Test Windows

The adaptive proportion, bucket, Markov, and external tests are evaluated over a configured window of incoming samples. Separate window sizes shall be configurable for:

- FIPS/conditioned mode, and
- Bypass mode.

The module shall select the correct window size based on the current operating mode. At the end of each window, the module shall generate a window-wrap event. Per-window test results shall be latched and compared against the active thresholds.

### 6.2 Thresholds

Each health test shall have separate high/low thresholds for FIPS and bypass modes. The module shall use the threshold set that matches the current mode.

### 6.3 Health-Test Failure Handling

If any health test fails:

- The module shall set a sticky failed-state indicator.
- The module shall increment the corresponding per-test total failure counter.
- The module shall increment the corresponding per-test alert failure counter.
- The module shall increment the overall alert failure counter.
- Entropy data associated with the failed window shall not be allowed to form a delivered seed.

The sticky failed-state indicator shall remain set until the next health-test window boundary or until the module is disabled.

All health-test counters shall be cleared when the module is re-enabled. The alert failure counters shall additionally be cleared by an explicit reset-alert-counters command from software.

If the overall alert failure count reaches the programmed alert threshold, and the threshold is nonzero, the module shall:

- Assert the health-test-failed interrupt.
- Assert a recoverable alert.
- Signal the main control logic to stop producing seeds from the failing data.

## 7. Conditioning and Seed Generation

In conditioned mode, health-tested entropy is accumulated in a pre-conditioning storage until enough words are available for the cryptographic conditioner. The conditioner shall produce 384-bit seeds.

The module shall apply backpressure to the upstream path when the conditioner is not ready. It shall not overrun the conditioner. A readiness masking mechanism shall prevent false ready indications from allowing data to be sent at the wrong time.

When the firmware override insertion path is used with the conditioner, firmware-written words shall be accumulated in the same pre-conditioning storage and then conditioned when the start control requests it.

In bypass mode, health-tested entropy is packed directly into 384-bit seeds without conditioning.

Complete seeds, along with their FIPS tag, shall be stored in the final seed storage. The final seed storage shall have a parameterizable depth; the default depth is four seeds. This storage shall backpressure the upstream data path when full.

## 8. Output Behavior

### 8.1 Hardware Entropy Interface

The hardware entropy interface uses a request/acknowledge handshake.

Behavior:

- When a request is asserted and a seed is available in final seed storage, the module shall present the 384-bit seed and its FIPS tag on the output and assert acknowledge.
- When a request is asserted but no seed is available, the module shall not assert acknowledge and shall wait.
- When software routing is selected, the hardware interface shall not be served.

### 8.2 Software Entropy Interface

When software routing is enabled, seeds from final seed storage are transferred to the software read FIFO. Firmware reads 32-bit words from the entropy data register. Each valid read shall pop the next 32-bit word from the software read FIFO. The module shall assert an interrupt when the software read FIFO is non-empty.

The software read FIFO shall be cleared when the module is disabled or when the software read path is disabled.

### 8.3 Bus Integrity Checking

The module shall monitor seeds as they are removed from final seed storage. It shall compare a portion of the current seed to the corresponding portion of the previous seed. If two consecutive removed seeds have identical captured portions, the module shall assert a recoverable alert. This check is intended to detect stuck or tampered entropy data.

## 9. Alert and Error Behavior

### 9.1 Recoverable Alerts

The module shall assert the recoverable alert output when any of the following conditions occurs:

- A security-sensitive configuration field has an invalid multi-bit encoding.
- The configured alert threshold and its inverse do not match.
- The main control state machine detects a health-test alert condition.
- The bus integrity check detects repeated seed data.
- Firmware attempts to write to the firmware insertion path while it is full.
- Firmware disables the SHA3 insertion operation while data remains in the pipeline.
- An external vendor health test reports a failure that contributes to the alert threshold.

The recoverable alert output shall also be generated when software writes to the recoverable alert test input.

### 9.2 Fatal Alerts

The module shall assert the fatal alert output when any of the following internal integrity conditions is detected:

- An internal FIFO protocol violation, such as attempting to read from an empty FIFO or an unexpected full condition.
- A main state machine or acknowledgment state machine error.
- A counter redundancy error.
- A conditioner storage or state error.
- A FIFO error that cannot be attributed to normal backpressure.

The module shall report the specific error source in error status registers. Fatal alert generation shall also be triggerable by the fatal alert test input from software.

### 9.3 Interrupts

The module shall provide four interrupt outputs:

1. **Entropy valid interrupt**: asserted when entropic data is available in the software read path.
2. **Health-test failed interrupt**: asserted when the health-test alert threshold condition is met.
3. **Observe FIFO ready interrupt**: asserted when the observation FIFO depth reaches the programmed threshold.
4. **Fatal error interrupt**: asserted when any fatal internal error condition is detected.

Each interrupt shall have an enable bit, a status bit, and a software test bit. The interrupt output shall be asserted only when the corresponding interrupt is enabled. The status bit shall remain set until cleared by software.

## 10. Disable and Re-enable Sequence

When firmware clears the module-enable field:

- The module shall immediately stop accepting new raw entropy from the RNG interface.
- The RNG enable output shall be deasserted.
- Entropy data already inside the pipeline may continue through health testing and conditioning so that in-flight operations can complete cleanly.
- The module shall not deliver new seeds to the hardware or software output paths after the disable command has taken effect.
- Final seed storage shall be cleared.
- Configuration writes shall remain locked until all internal activity has drained.
- The module shall expose a status indication that is set once it has fully drained and returned to idle.

Re-enabling the module shall be permitted only after the module has fully drained. On re-enable, the module shall clear all health-test state and counters before beginning normal operation.

## 11. Debug and Status Information

The module shall provide the following status information to firmware:

- Whether the main control state machine is idle.
- Whether the boot phase has completed.
- The current depth of the final seed storage.
- The current state of the cryptographic conditioner.
- Whether the conditioner has produced a valid output.
- Whether any fatal conditioner error has occurred.

This information is for software observation and is not required for normal operation.

## 12. External Vendor Health Test Interface

The module shall provide an external vendor health-test interface with the following behavior:

- The module shall output each raw entropy sample and a corresponding validity pulse to the external health-test block.
- The module shall output the health-test clear signal when health-test state is being reset.
- The module shall output the active indication to enable the external test whenever the module is running.
- The module shall output the selected high and low thresholds.
- The module shall output the window-wrap pulse at the end of each health-test window.
- The module shall output the current health-test window size and threshold-scope configuration.

The module shall receive from the external health-test block:

- High and low test count results.
- High and low failure pulses.
- A continuous-test indication.

If the external health-test block asserts the continuous-test indication, the module shall use the external test counts continuously rather than waiting for a window boundary.

Failure pulses from the external health-test block shall be included in the overall health-test failure accounting, alert counters, and health-test alert generation in the same manner as internal health-test failures.
